To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cholinergic stimulation of pancreatic acini causes protein phosphorylation via both the Ca2+ and the protein kinase C pathways, and that the two pathways act in a synergistic manner to stimulate pancreatic enzyme secretion.
the cholinergic secretagogues carbamoyl choline, bethanechol, and acetylcholine stimulate amylase release from mouse pancreatic acini by activating the phosphatidyl inositol pathway.

cholinergic stimulation of protein phosphorylation and amylase secretion in pancreatic acini is regulated by both Ca2+ and the diacylglyceride formed by phosphoinositide breakdown, and that synergism between the two intracellular messengers in regulating protein phosphorylation and secretion is of limited importance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Ca2+ as a second messenger in pancreatic acinar cells.
the role of protein phosphorylation and the intracellular messenger Ca2+ in the control of exocrine pancreatic secretion.
the regulation of pancreatic enzyme secretion and the role of protein phosphorylation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cholinergic stimulation of protein phosphorylation and amylase secretion is mediated by both diacylglycerylcerol and Ca2+.
the Ca2+ and phorbol esters act synergistically in regulating pancreatic protein phosphorylation and amylase release.
the Ca2+ and the DAG pathways are not synergistic in the control of enzyme secretion, and that the DAG pathway alone is sufficient for the activation of protein kinase C.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cholinergic stimulation of acinar cells results in an increase in the intracellular concentration of Ca2+ and in a decrease in the concentration of diacylglycerols.
Ca2+ and phorbol esters regulate distinct sets of proteins in pancreatic acini, but that synergistic effects are limited.

the phorbol myristate acetate and the Ca2+ channel agonist A23187 are not synergistic in stimulating pancreatic protein phosphorylation or amylase release, although the phorbol derivative is more effective than the ionophore in stimulating amylase secretion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a lot of variation in the effects of these agents in different species, and this is probably due to differences in the nature of the acinar cell receptors.
there are a lot of similarities between the way that the two different intracellular messengers act.
the phorbol-ester and ionophore are both effective in stimulating protein phosphorylation and acinar enzyme release, but the two agents are not synergistic in their action.
